title: Proportional Relationships
subtitle: Unit Rates, Constant k, Scale Drawings
bounds: T1: fractions a/b in simplest form, a < b, b in 2,3,4,5,6,8,10; the two denominators equal or one a multiple of the other; every cross product a×d and b×c a times-table fact (all four numbers ≤ 10); the unit rate is a whole number 2-10, a proper fraction (denominator ≤ 5) or a mixed number (whole part ≤ 4, fraction denominator ≤ 4); price items: one fractional lb, whole total 2-9, whole rate 2-10. T2-T4: x 1-10, k and every unit rate 2-10, table x values ≤ 9, every y ≤ 100, every × and ÷ a times-table fact. T5: scale k 2-10, drawn lengths 2-10, real lengths ≤ 100, rooms with real sides ≤ 10 (areas ≤ 100), area factor k×k ≤ 100. Distractors may be fractions or products over 100 (what the misreading gives).

tiers.name: Fraction Unit Rates
tiers.description: Find the rate per 1 when the amounts are fractions.

tiers.name: Proportional or Not?
tiers.description: Spot the equation, point or table where y is always k times x.

tiers.name: Finding the Constant k
tiers.description: Find k = y ÷ x from an equation, a point, a table or a story.

tiers.name: Write the Equation
tiers.description: Write y = kx from a story: totals, rates and unit conversions.

tiers.name: Scale Drawings
tiers.description: Scale lengths and areas up and down; areas scale by k × k.

INVERTED.student: Divided the wrong way. Per 1 means: divide by the 'per' amount.
INVERTED.teacher: Inverts the rate: time ÷ amount, x ÷ y or drawn ÷ real instead of amount ÷ time.

MULTIPLIED.student: Per 1 means divide. Dividing by a fraction makes the answer bigger.
MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies the two fractions (or the price and the fraction) instead of dividing.

FLIPPED_BOTH.student: Flip only the second fraction, then multiply. Not both.
FLIPPED_BOTH.teacher: Inverts both fractions when dividing: (a/b) ÷ (c/d) done as (b/a) × (d/c).

DROP_DENOMS.student: The bottoms count: 1/4 hour is a quarter of an hour, not 1 hour.
DROP_DENOMS.teacher: Divides the numerators and ignores the denominators.

DIFFERENCE.student: A rate, or 'how many times', is a quotient. Divide; don't subtract.
DIFFERENCE.teacher: Subtracts the two quantities instead of dividing them.

PRODUCT.student: k is y ÷ x. Multiplying x and y gives something else.
PRODUCT.teacher: Multiplies x and y instead of dividing.

ADDITIVE.student: Scaling multiplies or divides. Adding or subtracting is not scaling.
ADDITIVE.teacher: Adds (or subtracts) the same amount instead of multiplying (or dividing) both quantities.

INVERSE.student: Same direction: if x goes down by a factor, y goes down by that factor too.
INVERSE.teacher: Treats the relationship as inverse variation: keeps x times y fixed instead of y ÷ x.

ADDS_CONSTANT.student: y = x + 4 adds the same amount. Proportional means multiply: y = kx.
ADDS_CONSTANT.teacher: Thinks an adding equation (y = x + k) is proportional.

HAS_START.student: y = 4x + 1 does not start at 0. Proportional means (0, 0) is on it.
HAS_START.teacher: Allows a nonzero starting amount in a proportional equation.

SWAPPED_XY.student: Swapped. y is the one that equals k times x, so y = kx.
SWAPPED_XY.teacher: Writes x = ky (or x = y + c) with the variables reversed; k turns into 1/k.

Y_AS_K.student: That is a y value, not k. Divide: k = y ÷ x.
Y_AS_K.teacher: Uses the first y value as the constant instead of y ÷ x.

Y_STEP.student: y goes up by that much, but x goes up too. k = y ÷ x.
Y_STEP.teacher: Uses the step in y between table rows as k.

PROP_ASSUMED.student: Check every pair. y ÷ x changes, so this is not proportional.
PROP_ASSUMED.teacher: Takes the first pair's ratio as k and never checks the rest of the table.

PLUS_AS_TIMES.student: The table adds the same amount each time: y = x + c, not y = cx.
PLUS_AS_TIMES.teacher: Reads the added amount as a multiplier.

KEEPS_VAR.student: k is only the number. Leave the letter off.
KEEPS_VAR.teacher: Gives the whole term (6x) as the constant of proportionality.

TOTAL_AS_RATE.student: That total is for all of them. The rate for 1 is total ÷ count.
TOTAL_AS_RATE.teacher: Uses the total as the multiplier instead of the unit rate.

COUNT_AS_RATE.student: That is how many there are. The rate for 1 is total ÷ count.
COUNT_AS_RATE.teacher: Uses the count as the unit rate.

SWAPPED_VARS.student: Backwards. The thing you are finding goes alone on the left.
SWAPPED_VARS.teacher: Reverses the roles of the variables: writes x = ky for y = kx.

DIVIDES.student: More time means more, so multiply the rate. Dividing makes it shrink.
DIVIDES.teacher: Writes the rate over the variable (k/x) instead of k times x.

SCALED_DOWN.student: The real thing is bigger than the drawing: multiply by the scale.
SCALED_DOWN.teacher: Divides the drawn length by the scale when converting to real size.

WRONG_WAY.student: Real to drawing: divide by the scale. The drawing is smaller.
WRONG_WAY.teacher: Multiplies when converting a real length to the drawing.

FACTOR_ONLY.student: That is just the scale. Use it to multiply (or divide) the length.
FACTOR_ONLY.teacher: Gives the scale factor itself as the answer.

LINEAR_AREA.student: Area has two sides to scale, so the scale counts twice: k × k.
LINEAR_AREA.teacher: Scales an area by k instead of k × k.

DRAWING_AREA.student: That is the area on the drawing. Scale each side up to get the real area.
DRAWING_AREA.teacher: Gives the drawing's area instead of the real area.

ACTUAL_AREA.student: That is the real area. The drawing is smaller: scale each side down.
ACTUAL_AREA.teacher: Gives the real area when the drawing's area is asked.

ACTUAL_AS_SCALE.student: That is the whole real length. The scale is the real length of 1 unit.
ACTUAL_AS_SCALE.teacher: Gives the real length as the scale instead of dividing by the drawn length.

ONE_SIDE.student: Scale both sides, not just one.
ONE_SIDE.teacher: Scales only one side of the rectangle.

CUBED.student: Area uses 2 lengths, not 3. Multiply the scale by itself once: k × k.
CUBED.teacher: Cubes the scale factor (volume thinking) for an area.

ADDED_SIDES.student: Each side is scaled and then multiplied: k × k, not k + k.
ADDED_SIDES.teacher: Doubles the scale factor (k + k) instead of squaring it.
